doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Dating the lessons and the 1950s popular music
summary: Fleming jokes about the date, then places his early lessons in the 1950s and the doo-wop of the time.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But during that time, because I was being taught how to play the chords, at the time what they call two-five. I didn’t know it was that. I didn’t know. I didn’t hear that until maybe I was college age. Two-five. That was just — I knew that that was a natural progression.
Yeah. So when your uncle was teaching you this in the beginning, what year was this? What years? About when? Come on. You can tell me.
2016. I was crawling. Milk was running out of the side of my mouth.
Because I want to know what would the music, the popular music at the time.
Okay. So you were hearing some doo-wop.
